transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble at work. It's really nothing terrible, just... well, I supervise a sales team, and lately I keep making these kind of dumb mistakes on the weekly sales reports. 

Like, I'll accidentally copy the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I'm supposed to be checking. And the embarrassing part is, I always think I went over it perfectly. I really do try to be careful, I promise I'm not just slacking off or anything. I double-check things, but the mistakes just sort of slip by me anyway, if that makes sense? 

Is... is that the kind of information you're looking for?
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I mean... I'm actually a pretty upbeat guy, I think. I still really enjoy all my usual stuff, you know, watching the game, hanging out with friends. I haven't been feeling hopeless or anything like that. 

I really hope I didn't make it sound like I was complaining too much or, um, depressed! It's really just those little mistakes at work that are bothering me. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you noticed any problems with staying focused or keeping things organized in parts of your life outside of work, like at home or during leisure activities?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? It's really nothing terrible, just, you know, normal busy life stuff. Like, I might forget to return a call from my attorney, or... well, sometimes I'll accidentally let a bill sit around until I get a late notice. Which I know sounds bad, but I promise I always pay it the second I see the reminder! I just sort of lose track of it until then. 

And, um, occasionally I'll forget to pick up something I told the kids I'd bring home for them. I always feel awful when that happens, but I try to make it up to them right away. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible. I really do try my best to stay on top of things at home, it just slips my mind sometimes. Is... is that the kind of stuff you were asking about?
Do you find it hard to stay focused or finish tasks that require you to think carefully for a long time, like reading, planning something out, or working on a project?

Um, no, I don't really think so. I mean, if I have to plan out the quarter's sales strategy or read through a new company policy, I just sit down and do it. It's probably not my absolute favorite part of the job, sure, but I don't find it super hard to stay focused on it or anything. 

I can definitely put my head down and grind through a long project if that's what's expected of me. I really do try to be diligent about putting in the effort for things like that, I promise. I hope that's a helpful answer? I just haven't really noticed that being a big issue for me.
Do you ever find it hard to stay seated or feel restless during meetings or when you need to relax at home, like when watching TV or reading?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little bit? But I think that's pretty normal, right? I mean, sitting through a really long meeting... it sometimes feels like, I don't know, like my body is sort of buzzing inside? 

I try really hard not to be disruptive, I promise. I'll just, you know, shift around in my chair a bit, or maybe tap my foot under the table where no one can see. Or if it gets to be too much, I'll just make up a quick excuse to get up and grab some water or use the restroom. Just to stretch my legs, you know? 

At home, I can usually relax, but... yeah, sometimes sitting still for a whole movie is a little tricky. But I don't think it's anything too extreme. I really try to keep it under control so I don't bother anyone else. Is... is that okay? Like, is that the kind of thing you're looking for?
Can you recall if you had similar issues with attention, organization, or restlessness when you were a child, like in school or during activities with friends?

Um, well... yeah, I guess so. I mean, I don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I was a good kid, I promise. But, um, my mom actually still brings it up sometimes. She likes to joke about these notes my teachers used to send home in elementary school. 

Apparently, they would say things like I rushed through my work, or... or that I'd lose my homework sometimes. Which, you know, kids do that, right? And I guess they also mentioned that I would talk out of turn a bit, or that I had a hard time staying in my seat unless they reminded me. 

But I wasn't trying to be a troublemaker, I swear! I just... I guess I had a lot of energy back then. And I always tried to do better when they corrected me. Does that make sense? I hope that answers what you were asking about.
Can you recall if these childhood issues with attention or restlessness were present before you turned 12 years old?

Um, yes, definitely. Those notes from my teachers... that was all in elementary school, so definitely before I was 12. Like, maybe second or third grade? 

I know I just mentioned it, but yeah, my mom still brings it up. Just little things, you know? Like rushing through my assignments or misplacing my homework folders. And the talking out of turn or needing reminders to stay in my chair... that was all back then. 

But I really did grow out of the worst of it as I got older, and I always wanted to be a good student for my teachers. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was totally out of control as a little kid? I was just a bit... spirited, I guess. Is that the right timeframe you were wondering about?
Do you feel that these attention or restlessness issues have significantly interfered with your success in school, work, or relationships over the years?

Um, well... I mean, I really try my best not to let it affect things too much. I always want to do a good job, you know? But... I guess maybe it has caused a few bumps along the way. 

Like at work... I'm a supervisor, and I try so hard to keep everything running smoothly for my team, but... well, my manager actually brought it up in my last formal review. Just, you know, some things falling through the cracks. It was really embarrassing, honestly. I felt terrible that they had to point it out. I promised them I'd work on it, and I really am trying. 

And at home... I guess it can be a little frustrating for my family, too. Sometimes I'll say I'm going to do something and then I just... I get sidetracked, or I forget. It causes some arguments because they feel like they can't count on me to follow through. Which breaks my heart, because I never want them to feel that way. I want to be reliable for them. 

I don't want you to think I'm completely failing at everything, though! I still manage to get by, mostly. It's just... maybe a little harder than it should be sometimes? Does that... is that the kind of interference you mean?

Would you say these attention and restlessness issues cause you noticeable difficulty in at least two major areas of life, like work and home, or have a clear negative impact on your daily functioning?

Um, well, I guess... yeah, if I really think about it, it is both of those places. Like I was just saying, it's... it's at work, with my manager putting it in that formal review, which, again, I'm really working hard to fix! And then at home, with the arguments and my family feeling like they can't count on me to follow through. 

So I suppose that is two different areas, right? Work and home? I don't mean to sound like my whole life is a mess, because it's really not! I still get things done, and I care a lot about my job and my family. It's just... those two areas are where the bumps are happening the most right now. Is that... is that enough to count as what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily while working on tasks, like being pulled away by thoughts, sounds, or things happening around you?

Um, well, I guess... sometimes? I mean, I really try to stay focused, especially when I'm reviewing my team's call notes or checking their numbers. I want to make sure I'm giving them the right feedback. 

But, um... yeah, sometimes if there's a conversation happening across the room, or even if I just have a random thought about something I need to do at home... it can pull me off track before I even realize I've stopped working. 

I always catch myself and get right back to it, though! I don't let it ruin the whole day or anything. It's just a little blip. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible supervisor? I really do care about my work. Does that make sense, what you were asking about?
